messages:
Sarah W: Hey team, customer AcmeMaps (Jamie) is hitting intermittent 5xx/timeout errors against hosted inference since ~10:30 PST. Says it spikes during map tile bulk generation and they see a billing token spike as SDK retries. Need repro + fast mitigation.

Jamie (AcmeMaps): yep — we saw ~15% of requests return 503 or just hang then timeout. Our SDK retried a few times because default retry settings. We ended up with double billing for some requests (we track token usage on our side). Happened around our hourly bulk job.

Devon: can you paste a curl or sdk snippet you used? any correlation with model or route?

Jamie (AcmeMaps): using python-sdk, calls to /v1/generate with model:redwood-open-7b, concurrency ~200, per-request timeout 30s. snippet:```python
from redwood import Redwood
c = Redwood(api_key="REDACTED")
resp = c.generate(model="redwood-open-7b", prompt="...", timeout=30)
```

Aisha: thanks. Do you have request-id headers from failures? Also any client logs showing retry attempts (timestamped) would help.

Jamie (AcmeMaps): got one example from logs: X-Request-Id: rwd_8f7a2b; response status 503; SDK did 3 retries (0.5s, 1s, 2s). we log tokens billed per success; not easy to tie partial failures.

Devon: initial thought — retry loop on transient edge errors causing duplicate attempts and token spikes. We should capture a tcpdump + gateway logs. @oncall-bot can you add incident tag?

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1839. Pager duty alerted to @eng-runtime oncall.

Ken (Eng Runtime): looking. Can someone dump the exact request-ids and approximate times? I’ll grep the edge logs for 503 signatures and upstream DNS errors.

Sarah W: Provided three request ids to Ken in DM (rwd_8f7a2b, rwd_8f9c1f, rwd_8fae33). Jamie says spike window 10:28–10:40 PST.

Marta (SRE): I see a pattern in front-proxy logs — a cluster of upstream connect errors to model-backend pool in that window. Not classic cpu OOM, looks like short DNS resolution failures (NXDOMAIN/timeout) at our edge cluster for a subset of nodes. That would return 503 to clients.

Ken (Eng Runtime): confirm — edge tried to resolve backend host, got temporary SERVFAIL for 15s for some nodes, then retries to different host. SDK retries compound the issue because some calls succeeded on retry.

Devon: OK that meshes with customer pattern: intermittent 503 + SDK three retries -> double/triple billing attempts when the later retry succeeds. We should advise customer to reduce retry count short-term, and we should consider idempotency header handling to avoid billing duplicates.

Aisha: Jamie — temporary mitigation for you: set max_retries=1 in SDK and increase client-side request timeout to 60s so you don't trigger multiple quick retries. Also include a client-generated idempotency key (e.g., Idempotency-Key: <uuid>) on non-streaming generate calls if you can — that will let us dedupe on our end where supported.

Jamie (AcmeMaps): can do. How quickly can you confirm the root cause? Customer is nervous about ongoing billing discrepancies.

Ken (Eng Runtime): I'm escalating to infra/SRE — looks like our internal resolver cluster had a short window of degraded responses due to a misconfigured node rotation. Marta is taking lead on rollback.

Marta (SRE): rolling back the last dns-proxy config change on the affected region now. ETA ~10m. We'll monitor for broken resolvers and proxy health.

oncall-bot: Deploy rollback started: deploy-rollback/2026-03-15-1012 by Marta.

Devon: In parallel we should add a gateway safeguard: when upstream returns connect errors, classify them as transient and respond with 502+Retry-After? But for immediate fix, we can add request de-dup using Idempotency-Key header for generate endpoints (short TTL) to avoid charging multiple times for retries that eventually succeed. Ken, can you scope?

Ken (Eng Runtime): can prototype a short-lived in-memory dedupe keyed by Idempotency-Key + payload hash for 60s. Low-risk config change. I'll open an RFC and a small canary patch to gateway today.

Sarah W: Communication to customer — Aisha, can you post an interim update recommending the SDK config change and ask them to hold billing disputes until we confirm rollback? Also offer one-time credit if duplicate billing confirmed.

Aisha: on it. Draft message to Jamie: "We're seeing short DNS resolver errors causing 503s for a small fraction of requests in your region. Immediate steps: set max_retries=1 and timeout=60s, add Idempotency-Key for critical requests. We're rolling back the resolver change now and will monitor. If you see duplicate billing tied to our retries we'll issue a credit. ETA for rollback 10m."

Jamie (AcmeMaps): thanks — applying SDK changes now. will report back in 15m. Appreciate the rapid response.

Marta (SRE): rollback complete. Watching edge health. Initial metrics show 503 rate down to baseline within 2 minutes.

Ken (Eng Runtime): opened PR for dedupe: rwd/gateway#542 — simple in-memory cache TTL=60s, respects Idempotency-Key and payload hash. Will canary in eu-west-1.

Devon: Nice. Once canary is green, we should wire in billing-side dedupe or at least surface duplicate billing events to support.

Aisha: Jamie — can you confirm after applying SDK changes whether you still see 503s or billing spikes?

Jamie (AcmeMaps): quick update — after SDK tweak (max_retries=1) failures in the last 20m dropped to near zero and no unexpected token charge spikes yet. We'll keep monitoring next hourly job. Thanks.

Sarah W: I'll keep thread open until next daily check. Closing notes for postmortem: root cause = resolver rotation bug causing transient SERVFAIL; customer impact = intermittent 503 + SDK retry amplification -> billing duplicates; mitigations = rollback, recommend client SDK config + idempotency, gateway dedupe PR.

Ken (Eng Runtime): assign follow-up: PR review, canary, telemetry to detect duplicate-success-after-5xx patterns.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-1839 status: mitigated.

Sarah W: Thanks everyone — I'll send customer the formal summary and a gesture for duplicate charges if any surface. Closing in 24h if no recurrence.

Jamie (AcmeMaps): all good for now. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
